text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthDrinking Tea May Reduce Vascular Disease RiskBut there’s a catchJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CDT on October 21, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe enduring global popularity of tea may represent a humiliating cultural defeat for the United States, but ultimately it’s for the best. That’s because tea contains loads of compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity and may even benefit gut microbiomes. Now, a new study on the health benefits of the world’s favorite flavored beverage may make my fellow Americans reconsider it. Powered By 10 ShareNextStayA team of medical researchers led by medical experts from the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences followed the health of nearly half a million people between the ages of 30 and 79 enrolled in the China Kadoorie Biobank for a period of roughly nine years. In addition to monitoring their health, the Biobank collected data on the subjects’ tea-drinking habits, including daily number of cups, preferred temperature and type, and even strength.
